The All India Engineering Entrance Examination (AIEEE) was India's flagship national entrance exam conducted between 2002 and 2012 for admission to NITs (formerly RECs), IIITs, Deemed Universities, and Central/State Government Technical Institutes. From 2013 onward, AIEEE was replaced by JEE Main under the "One Nation, One Test" reform.

blocks.p: JEE Main is administered across multiple sessions out of 300 marks (75 questions of 4 marks each; 25 per subject). Normalized percentile scores map test-takers across shifts to determine eligibility for Top NITs, IIITs, GFTIs, and eligibility for JEE Advanced. Because candidate volume has expanded from roughly 11–12 lakh test-takers in the late 2010s to over 14–15 lakh candidates in recent cycles, raw marks corresponding to a given percentile have risen in moderate- difficulty shifts. Top NIT admissions depend heavily on both All India Rank (AIR) and Home State versus Other State quotas.

blocks.p: Conducted for the top 2.5 lakh qualifiers of JEE Main. Maximum aggregate marks vary each year (historically between 360 and 396 marks across Paper 1 and Paper 2). iit-jee.intro: Simple, table-by-table reference covering exam evolution, question patterns, candidate numbers, fees, seat matrix, and the 16 IITs before JEE Advanced began in 2013. The Indian Institute of Technology Joint Entrance Examination (IIT-JEE) was conducted for over five decades ( 1961 to 2012 ) as the direct single-tier admission test for undergraduate programmes at the IITs, IT-BHU (now IIT BHU), and ISM Dhanbad. Unlike today's system where JEE Main filters candidates first, any eligible Class 12 student could directly write IIT-JEE until 2012. In 2013, IIT-JEE was replaced by JEE Advanced.

table: IIT-JEE — Indian Institute of Technology Joint Entrance Examination
Joint Admission Board (JAB) — Conducted by one of the older zonal IITs each year on rotation (IIT Bombay, Delhi, Guwahati, Kanpur, Kharagpur, Madras, Roorkee)
Conducted from 1961 to 2012 (52 years). Replaced by JEE Advanced starting in 2013.
Once a year (held on a Sunday in April; from 2000–2005 it had a Screening + Main two-stage format)
Offline Pen-and-Paper (Objective OMR sheets from 2006–2012; subjective descriptive papers prior to 2006). Printed in English and Hindi.
Paper 1 (3 Hours, Morning) + Paper 2 (3 Hours, Afternoon) on the same day. Both papers tested Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.
From 2006 onward: Maximum 2 consecutive attempts (Class 12 appearing year + next year) and minimum 60% aggregate in Class 12 boards (55% for SC/ST/PwD).

sections.h: Exam Overview & Basic Facts

blocks.p: IIT-JEE went through three distinct historical eras in how questions were asked—moving from 3-hour descriptive subjective papers to a two-stage Screening + Main exam, and finally to the fully objective 6- hour OMR format (2006–2012):

sections.h: Question Paper Pattern & How IIT-JEE Evolved

table: 4 separate papers: Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and English (English was dropped later). Long step-by- step subjective derivations and numerical proofs graded manually by IIT professors.
Screening: 1 single 3-hour MCQ paper (PCM) to shortlist ~20,000 candidates. Main: 3 separate 2-hour subjective papers (Physics, Chemistry, Maths) for final rank.
Two 3-hour objective OMR papers on the same day (6 hours total). Machine-graded optical bubble sheets with negative marking and partial marking.

blocks.p: Candidates who clear the written exam are called to a Services Selection Board (SSB) centre (Allahabad, Bhopal, Bengaluru, Kapurthala, Varanasi, Mysuru, Gandhinagar, or Dehradun) for a 5-day personality assessment:

table: Verbal/Non-Verbal Intelligence Test + Picture Perception & Discussion Test. ~50–60% candidates are screened out on Day 1; the rest stay for Days 2–5.
Stage II — Psychological Tests (TAT, WAT, SRT, SD)
Story writing on 12 pictures (TAT), 60-word association (WAT), 60 real-life situations (SRT), and Self-Description (SD) tested by a Psychologist.
Group Discussion, Group Planning Exercise (GPE), Progressive & Half Group Tasks, Individual Obstacles, Command Task, and 3-minute Lecturette.
One-on-one rapid-fire and situational interview with the Interviewing Officer covering academics, family, hobbies, and current affairs.
All three assessors (Psychologist, GTO, Interviewing Officer) review your 15 Officer-Like Qualities (OLQs) and announce recommended candidates.

blocks.p: Air Force Flying Extra Test (CPSS): Candidates who opt for the Air Force Flying Branch and get recommended by SSB must also pass the Computerised Pilot Selection System (CPSS) and PABT (conducted only once in a lifetime).

table: Fee, Stipend & Pay Details (7th Pay Commission)
100% Free Training: Government pays for accommodation, food, uniforms, books, and medical care (only minor pocket-money deposit required).
Cadets receive a fixed training stipend of ₹56,100 per month throughout the final year.
Basic Pay ₹56,100 + Military Service Pay (MSP) ₹15,500 + DA & Allowances = ₹1,00,000 – ₹1,20,000 / month in-hand.
Basic Pay ₹56,100 + MSP ₹15,500 + Sea/Submarine Allowances = ₹1,00,000 – ₹1,25,000 / month in-hand.
Basic Pay ₹56,100 + MSP ₹15,500 + Flying Allowance (up to ₹25,000) = ₹1,15,000 – ₹1,40,000 / month in-hand.

table: Apply on upsconline.nic.in (December for NDA-I in April; May for NDA-II in September). Select service preferences carefully.
Attempt Maths (120 Qs in 150 mins) and GAT (150 Qs in 150 mins) on the same day. Focus on accuracy to avoid 1/3rd negative marks.
Within 3–4 weeks, UPSC publishes roll numbers of qualified candidates. Register on the service portal and pick your SSB interview date.
Attend SSB (travel allowance for AC-3 tier train is reimbursed for first-timers). If recommended, undergo a 5–7 day Military Hospital medical checkup.
UPSC combines Written + SSB scores (out of 1,800). Selected candidates receive joining instructions for NDA Khadakwasla (January or July term).
